thread:
Priya: Heads-up — getting a flood of pagers for /v1/generate SLOs, started ~22:14 UTC. 5xx spike + p95 latency creeping above 2s for a subset of requests. Not seeing user error pages yet but oncall alerts are noisy.

incident-bot: [ALERT] generate_slo violated (service=/v1/generate, window=5m, breach=1.8%). Alert ID: ALT-20260314-71. Pager sent to @eng-oncall rotation.

Sam: I'm primary for this shift, taking lead. @Leah you still secondary? @Matt can you stand by for infra help?

Leah: Yep I'm secondary, on it. I'll try to correlate with the model rollout logs.

Priya: Pasting a snippet from the logs — lots of `kvmcache` misses and repeated 503s from the serving tier: ```
[22:12:43] upstream error: connection reset by peer (serving-node-17)
[22:12:44] 503 POST /v1/generate model=redwood-large-v2-8q variant=8q user=svc-ingest
[22:12:45] kv-cache miss id=0x4f12f keylen=128
```

Matt: That looks like KV cache pressure + transient OOMs we've seen on the 8q quantized variant. No config changes deployed in the last hour AFAIK. Could be a background reclaim job.

Sam: Quick mitigation options: 1) suppress noisy SLO alert for a short window; 2) route traffic off the 8q variant to the fallback warm variant; 3) reboot the affected serving node if infra confirms OOM. Thoughts?

Leah: I can apply a narrow suppression scoped to the generate_slo alert and only for the next 20m while we validate. Per runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/slo-alert-suppression (see "temporary threshold raise" section).

Priya: Routing off 8q would be safer if autoscaling + fallback is healthy. We have a policy `route: model_fallback` that can be toggled in the router. It will increase cost though.

Matt: Infra confirms one node (serving-node-17) had repeated OOMs, they removed a stray background job (db-consolidator). I'm going to bring the node to draining state and spin up a replacement. ETA 6-8m.

Sam: Ok plan: Leah apply suppression for 20m, Matt drain and replace node, Priya monitor error rate and p95. If errors persist after 20m, we'll route traffic off 8q. Also add a note to escalation if suppression needs extension.

Leah: Applying suppression now: `opsctl alerts suppress --alert generate_slo --duration 20m --reason "mid-shift noisy SLO during node replacement"`

incident-bot: Suppression applied by Leah (20m). Suppression ID: SUP-3301.

Priya: Monitoring graphs — error rate dropped from 1.8% to 0.6% after node drain started. p95 back down to ~1.1s.

Sam: Great. No external customer impact observed (no 5xx increase in our front door logs). We'll keep an eye for recurrence.

Matt: Node replacement finished, health checks back green on the new instance.

Leah: Suppression will auto-expire in 12m. I'll add a follow-up message before expiry to decide rollback or extend.

Sam: Hand-off note for the next shift: check `generate_slo` alert state, confirm SUP-3301 expired, and validate serving-node fleet stable for the last 30m. If error rate bumps >1% re-open and consider temporary routing off variant 8q.

Priya: Filing a short incident note in #incidents after this thread, flagging the db-consolidator job that leaked memory.

Matt: +1. Also add a short item to postmortem: consider adding a circuit-breaker for KV-cache pressure to avoid SLO noise.

Leah: Copy that. I'll update the runbook with the suppression command and variant-routing steps.

Sam: Thanks team. I'll mark this as monitored and close the thread if nothing else triggers in the next 20m. :white_check_mark:
